definition: A database engineered specifically to store, index, and query high-dimensional embeddings using Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search algorithms.
details: Vector databases leverage graph-based (e.g., HNSW) or inverted-file quantization (e.g., IVF-PQ) structures to execute similarity search over millions of high-dimensional vectors within millisecond constraints.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. In plain words: A database engineered specifically to store, index, and query high-dimensional embeddings using Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search algorithms. Here is how it actually plays out: Vector databases leverage graph-based (e.g., HNSW) or inverted-file quantization (e.g., IVF-PQ) structures to execute similarity search over millions of high-dimensional vectors within millisecond constraints. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. That care with the raw material is Vector Database.
